content: Formoterol is a medication used to treat wheezing, shortness of breath, and breathing difficulties caused by asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), which includes chronic bronchitis and emphysema. It is also used to prevent exercise-induced bronchospasm. Formoterol belongs to a class of medications called long-acting beta agonists (LABAs). It works by relaxing and opening the air passages in the lungs, making it easier to breathe. Important Warning: In a large clinical study, more patients who used a medication similar to formoterol died from asthma-related problems compared to those who did not use the medication. If you have asthma, using formoterol may increase the risk of experiencing serious or fatal asthma problems. Your doctor will only prescribe formoterol if other medications have not adequately controlled your asthma or if your asthma is so severe that two medications are required to manage it. Formoterol should not be the first or only medication used to treat asthma. Do not use formoterol if your asthma is rapidly worsening. Inform your doctor if you have had frequent severe asthma attacks or if you have ever been hospitalized due to asthma symptoms. If you notice any of the following signs of worsening asthma, contact your doctor immediately: Your short-acting inhaler is less effective than before. You need to use more puffs or use your short-acting inhaler more frequently. You use four or more puffs per day of your short-acting inhaler for two or more consecutive days. You use more than one canister (200 inhalations) of your short-acting inhaler within an eight-week period. Your peak flow meter shows worsening breathing. You need to visit the emergency room for asthma treatment. Your symptoms do not improve after using formoterol regularly for one week, or your symptoms worsen at any time during treatment. Discuss the risks of using this medication with your doctor. Your doctor or pharmacist will provide you with a Medication Guide when you start treatment with formoterol and each time you refill your prescription. Read the information carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. You can also visit the FDA website or the manufacturer’s website for the Medication Guide. How to Use This Medication: Formoterol comes as a powder-filled capsule to inhale using a special inhaler. If you are using formoterol to treat asthma or COPD, you will likely inhale it twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening. Always inhale your next dose 12 hours after your last dose, and try to use it at the same times every day. If you are using formoterol to prevent exercise-induced breathing difficulties, inhale it at least 15 minutes before exercise, but do not use it more than once every 12 hours. If you are using formoterol twice daily on a regular basis, do not take an additional dose before exercising. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to explain any part you do not understand. Use formoterol exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it or use it more often than prescribed by your doctor. Discuss with your doctor how to take your other oral or inhaled asthma medications during your treatment with formoterol. If you were taking a corticosteroid to prevent airway swelling, your doctor will likely instruct you to continue taking it as before. If you were using a short-acting beta agonist inhaler regularly, your doctor will likely tell you to stop using it regularly but to continue using it for sudden asthma symptoms. Formoterol helps prevent asthma or COPD attacks but will not stop an attack that has already started. Do not use formoterol during an asthma or COPD attack. Your doctor will prescribe a short-acting inhaler for use during attacks. Formoterol controls the symptoms of asthma and other lung diseases but does not cure these conditions. Do not stop using formoterol without consulting your doctor, as your symptoms may worsen. If you stop using formoterol suddenly, your symptoms may worsen. Before using the formoterol inhaler for the first time, ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to show you how to use it. Practice using the inhaler while they observe. Follow the specific steps provided for using the inhaler, including proper storage and handling of the capsules. Do not use the inhaler to inhale any other type of capsules. Special Precautions: Before using formoterol: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to formoterol, any other medications, or milk proteins. Tell your doctor if you are using another LABA, such as fluticasone and salmeterol combination (Advair) or salmeterol (Serevent). These medications should not be used with formoterol. Your doctor will advise you on which medication to use and which to stop. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Certain medications may interact with formoterol, and your doctor may need to adjust your doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had an irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, seizures, diabetes, or heart or thyroid disease. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using formoterol, contact your doctor. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Formoterol may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of these symptoms are severe or persistent: Nervousness Headache Uncontrollable shaking of a body part Dry mouth Muscle cramps Back pain Nausea Heartburn Stomach pain Extreme tiredness Dizziness Difficulty falling or staying asleep Stuffy or runny nose Sore throat Severe Side Effects: Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience: Swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs Hoarseness Difficulty swallowing or breathing Hives Rash Fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat Chest pain Lightheadedness Fainting Formoterol may cause other side effects. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication. Storage Instructions: Keep formoterol capsules sealed in their blister cards until ready for use. Store the medication at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly, and replace your inhaler with each prescription refill. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal methods. In Case of Emergency/Overdose: In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include: Chest pain Fainting Fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeat Nervousness Headache Uncontrollable shaking of a body part Seizures Muscle cramps Dry mouth Nausea Dizziness Excessive tiredness Difficulty falling or staying asleep Thirst Trouble breathing Additional Information: Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
